The thinnest read in the batch and honestly labelled as such. What is on Drive is the covering report only; every number is in Appendix A, which we do not hold, so there is no CFR, no borrowing position and no reconciliation.

The one thing we can say comes from our own PWLB file rather than their paper: a single loan, £5m at 4.59%, which matured on 1 May 2026, and nothing since. If that is right North Norfolk holds no PWLB debt at all, which would make the investment half of Appendix A the entire story. That is framed to them as ours to be corrected on.

Contact is good — James Moore, named as contact officer with an address. Fetching Appendix A would turn this from a courtesy note into a real one.

officer.body:
Hi James,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. Normally that means we write with something specific about a council's own numbers. This one is shorter and more honest than most, because what we can see of your outturn report is the covering report only — Appendix A, where all the figures live, isn't in what we hold. So nothing below is a comment on your position, and we haven't guessed at one.

The one thing we can offer runs the other way, from our data to you. Our PWLB file shows a single loan for North Norfolk — £5m at 4.59%, loan 821308, matured 1 May 2026 — and nothing since. Taken at face value that would mean no PWLB debt outstanding at all, which would put you in a small group of districts and make the investment side of Appendix A the whole story. We hold PWLB only, so market debt, bank loans and anything drawn from other authorities sit outside our file entirely, and Appendix A will say what our data cannot. What we hold for you is visible at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis.

For context on the market you're lending into rather than borrowing from: Bank Rate is 3.75%, one-year PWLB certainty closed at 4.95% this afternoon on notice 314/26, and July's sector borrowing was £368m across 33 loans from just 19 borrowers at an average 5.02% — a thin market, which is itself informative if you're pricing deposits with other authorities. That monthly breakdown is at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity.

On training, three would fit. Liability Benchmark: the essentials, which is the indicator most likely to matter to a council with little or no debt and a capital programme ahead of it. Money Market Funds (CNAV / LVNAV / VNAV), for the investment side. And Audit committee scrutiny for members, given this report goes through Governance, Risk and Audit before Full Council. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Source: Treasury Outturn Report 2025/26 (covering report), Council, 17 June 2026.
